title: Combination antiviral treatment for a patient with lymphocytic choriomeningitis virus meningoencephalitis associated with bispecific antibody teclistamab therapy for myeloma

analysis.scope_and_question: Lymphocytic choriomeningitis virus (LCMV) is a rare cause of meningoencephalitis in humans. The review focuses on the clinical presentation and management of LCMV meningoencephalitis in a patient with relapsed multiple myeloma receiving teclistamab therapy.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The evidence is derived from a single case report. Metagenomic next-generation sequencing of cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) was used to identify LCMV. The patient's history of domestic rodent exposure was also noted. No meta-analysis or pooled estimates were reported.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: LCMV meningoencephalitis is self-limiting in immunocompetent individuals but can cause severe disease in immunocompromised hosts. The case report shows that combination antiviral therapy with ribavirin, remdesivir, and molnupiravir led to sustained neurological improvement, with LCMV clearance from CSF and blood within 2 months. Antiviral therapy was continued for 6 months.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review highlights the lack of reported UK cases of LCMV in humans since the 1950s, and the rarity of testing for LCMV. The case report provides preliminary evidence for combination antiviral therapy in persistent LCMV infection, but further studies are needed to confirm its efficacy.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The case underscores the importance of metagenomic next-generation sequencing in diagnosing LCMV in undiagnosed encephalitis. It also suggests the need for further research on the role of combination antiviral therapy in managing persistent LCMV infection, particularly in immunocompromised patients.

analysis.summary_en: This review reports a case of lymphocytic choriomeningitis virus (LCMV) meningoencephalitis in a patient with relapsed multiple myeloma receiving teclistamab. LCMV is a rare cause of meningoencephalitis in humans, with no UK cases reported since the 1950s. The patient, who was immunocompromised, showed severe neurological symptoms, and combination antiviral therapy with ribavirin, remdesivir, and molnupiravir led to sustained improvement. The case highlights the utility of metagenomic next-generation sequencing for LCMV detection and suggests preliminary support for combination antiviral therapy in persistent infections. However, the rarity of LCMV cases and the need for more research on its management in immunocompromised hosts remain significant evidence gaps.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to evaluate the diagnostic performance of a new single-reaction RT-PCR assay for Lassa virus in Sierra Leone, where molecular diagnosis is complicated by the virus's genetic diversity and limited laboratory capacity.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study conducted a diagnostic evaluation of the PANDAA Lassa Virus RT-PCR assay using 94 archived serum samples from Sierra Leone, with 79 samples having valid paired results.
analysis.methods: The PANDAA assay was compared to the dual-target RealStar(C) Lassa Virus RT-PCR Kit 2.0 using 94 archived serum samples from Sierra Leone, with agreement metrics calculated for both assays.
analysis.main_results: The PANDAA assay demonstrated a positive percent agreement of 78.12% (95% CI 61.25%-88.98%), a negative percent agreement of 93.62% (95% CI 82.84%-97.81%), and an overall agreement of 87.34% (95% CI 78.24%-92.98%) with the RealStar(C) assay, and a Cohen's kappa of 0.73 (95% CI 0.58-0.89).

title: Diagnostic accuracy of a single-reaction, pan-lineage Lassa virus RT-PCR at two Nigerian laboratories: a retrospective and prospective cohort study

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the challenge of developing a single-reaction RT-PCR assay capable of detecting all Lassa virus variants with equal sensitivity due to its intra- and inter-lineage nucleotide diversity.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A retrospective and prospective cohort study was conducted using plasma samples from patients with suspected Lassa fever at two Nigerian laboratories: Abubakar Tafawa Balewa University Teaching Hospital in Bauchi and Federal Medical Centre in Owo.
analysis.methods: The study compared the diagnostic accuracy of PANDAA(R) LASV, a single-reaction pan-lineage RT-PCR assay, with the RealStar(R) Lassa Virus RT-PCR Kit 2.0, the current diagnostic standard in Nigeria. Ct values were analyzed for correlation with reference assay targets, and performance was assessed across sites.
analysis.main_results: PANDAA(R) LASV demonstrated a sensitivity of 98.6% (138/140; 95% CI 94.9-99.8%), specificity of 99.4% (155/156; 96.5-100%), and accuracy of 99.0% (293/296; 97.1-99.8%). Three confirmed discordant results occurred at high Ct values near assay detection limits.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study concluded that PANDAA(R) LASV has high diagnostic accuracy compared to the dual-reaction reference assay, maintaining equivalent sensitivity and specificity while reducing the operational burden.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that adopting PANDAA(R) LASV could reduce labor and reagent costs and improve turnaround time for Lassa fever diagnosis in Nigerian laboratories.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study had a limited sample size and relied on existing specimens, which may affect generalizability. However, performance was consistent across sites with overlapping confidence intervals, indicating moderate evidence strength.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the diagnostic accuracy of PANDAA(R) LASV, a single-reaction pan-lineage RT-PCR assay, in detecting Lassa virus compared to the dual-reaction RealStar(R) Lassa Virus RT-PCR Kit 2.0 at two Nigerian laboratories. The study used both retrospective and prospective plasma samples from patients with suspected Lassa fever. PANDAA(R) LASV showed high sensitivity (98.6%), specificity (99.4%), and accuracy (99.0%), with performance consistent across sites. The positive likelihood ratio was 153.8 (21.8-1084.9) and the negative likelihood ratio was 0.01 (0.00-0.06). Three discordant results occurred at high Ct values near detection limits. The study highlights the potential of PANDAA(R) LASV to reduce operational costs and improve diagnostic efficiency. However, the study's reliance on existing specimens and limited sample size may affect generalizability, resulting in moderate evidence strength.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Junin virus (JUNV) is a causative agent of Argentine Hemorrhagic Fever (AHF) in humans (especially in farmers) with no long-term approved antiviral therapeutics. The study aimed to design a multi-epitope vaccine against JUNV using immunoinformatics.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study was conducted using an immunoinformatics approach comprising sequence retrieval, epitope prediction, vaccine design and analysis, molecular docking, MD simulations, immune simulation, and in silico cloning. The vaccine was evaluated for its properties such as antigenicity, allergenicity, membrane localization, and toxicity.
analysis.methods: The vaccine was designed using immunoinformatics methods, including sequence retrieval, epitope prediction, and analysis. It was linked by β-defensin 3 and a PADRE sequence at both termini and multiple structural linkers to ensure stability and proper epitope spacing. Molecular docking and MD simulations were used to assess the vaccine's structural and dynamic behavior.
analysis.main_results: The designed vaccine showed a worldwide population coverage (98.83%), antigenic (0.8295) non-allergenic, outside membrane, and non-toxic properties. Structural assessment revealed an ERRAT score of 94.758%, with 93.8% residues in the favored region of the Ramachandran plot and a ProSA Z-score of -6.3.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as indicating that the vaccine has favorable properties for potential immunity against JUNV. The novelty lies in the use of immunoinformatics-driven multi-epitope vaccine design for JUNV.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that the vaccine could be a promising candidate for preventing Argentine Hemorrhagic Fever, offering potential for surveillance, diagnosis, and future vaccine development.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to in silico methods, and in vitro or in vivo studies are necessary to confirm its efficacy. The evidence is moderate as it relies on computational models rather than experimental validation.

analysis.summary_en: This study presents an immunoinformatics-driven multi-epitope vaccine design against Junin virus (JUNV), the causative agent of Argentine Hemorrhagic Fever (AHF). The vaccine was developed using sequence retrieval, epitope prediction, molecular docking, MD simulations, immune simulation, and in silico cloning. The results indicate that the vaccine has high worldwide population coverage, is antigenic, non-allergenic, outside membrane, and non-toxic. Structural assessment showed favorable properties with an ERRAT score of 94.758%, 93.8% residues in the favored region of the Ramachandran plot, and a ProSA Z-score of -6.3. The vaccine's predicted binding affinity with human TLR2 was higher than with TLR4, and immune simulation suggested enhanced humoral and cellular responses. The authors concluded that the vaccine shows potential immunity against JUNV, though further in vitro or in vivo studies are needed to confirm its efficacy. The study's evidence is moderate due to its reliance on computational methods without experimental validation.

title: Viral Infection Across the Kidney Transplant Continuum: Screening, Prevention, Management, and Oncogenesis

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the impact of viral infections across the kidney transplantation continuum, focusing on immunologic risk, graft outcomes, and long-term patient survival. Viral infections influence every stage, from pre-transplant serologic assessments to post-transplant morbidity and oncogenesis.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study design involved pre-transplant serologic assessments and post-transplant surveillance for viral pathogens in kidney transplant recipients. The population included transplant recipients and donors, with a focus on viral infections and their complications.
analysis.methods: Methods included pre-transplant serologic assessments, post-transplant surveillance for viral pathogens, and acceptance of hepatitis C viremic donor organs. The study also considered the impact of donor-derived viral infections, including rabies, West Nile virus, and lymphocytic choriomeningitis virus.
analysis.main_results: Post-transplant, viral pathogens such as CMV and BK virus were major drivers of morbidity. Persistent viral infections and virus-associated glomerulopathies contributed to chronic graft loss, while EBV-driven post-transplant lymphoproliferative disorder remained a significant cause of cancer-related mortality.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings, highlighting the importance of routine surveillance for CMV and BK viremia, and the association of viral infections with progressive allograft dysfunction and malignancies. Novel insights included the role of persistent HPV infection in anogenital and oropharyngeal malignancies.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings have specific implications for surveillance, diagnosis, and management of viral infections in kidney transplant recipients, emphasizing the need for targeted interventions to reduce morbidity and improve graft survival.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study design limitations included the lack of randomization and the potential for confounding factors. The evidence strength was moderate, given the observational nature of the study and the need for further research to establish causality.

analysis.summary_en: This study examined the impact of viral infections across the kidney transplantation continuum, highlighting the role of CMV, BK virus, and HPV in morbidity and graft loss. The findings emphasize the need for routine surveillance and targeted interventions to improve patient outcomes.

title: 773 Identification of novel therapeutic targets on tumor-infiltrating regulatory T cells using an in vivo CRISPR screening system

analysis.research_question_and_background: Regulatory T (Treg) cells are abundant in tumor tissues and play key roles in facilitating immune evasion by tumor cells.
analysis.study_design_and_population: Targeting tumor-infiltrating Treg cells specifically while sparing peripheral Treg cells is a promising strategy in immunotherapy. To increase the number of thymus-derived SMARTA Treg cells in TCR-transgenic mice, expression of full-length LCMV-GP driven by the rat insulin promoter and administration of IL-2 complexes were utilized.
analysis.methods: Genomic DNA was extracted and subjected to sequencing, with sgRNA abundance as the readout. In parallel with the CRISPR screen, an in vivo suppression assay was developed to validate the function of individual genes.
analysis.main_results: Antigen expression and IL-2 complex treatment increased SMARTA Treg cell numbers by more than fivefold. In vivo CRISPR screening using the library revealed that several known Treg cell regulators, including Il2ra and Icos, were among the top hits, validating the model.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: In addition, Rgs16 (Log[fold-change] = -1.06) and Anxa2 (Log[fold-change] = -0.77) emerged as candidate regulators of Treg cell abundance.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: We established an in vivo CRISPR screening platform to identify novel therapeutic targets in tumor-infiltrating Treg cells for improving immunotherapy outcomes.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The supplied evidence does not report limitations or evidence strength.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to identify novel therapeutic targets on tumor-infiltrating regulatory T cells to improve immunotherapy outcomes. The researchers employed an in vivo CRISPR screening system using monoclonal SMARTA Treg cells specific to glycoprotein (GP) 61–80 of lymphocytic choriomeningitis virus (LCMV) to explore gene regulation in these cells. They increased the number of SMARTA Treg cells in TCR-transgenic mice by expressing full-length LCMV-GP and administering IL-2 complexes. The CRISPR library targeted 34 genes more highly expressed in tumor-infiltrating Treg cells than in peripheral Treg cells. SMARTA Treg cells were adoptively transferred to mice bearing MC38 tumors overexpressing LCMV-GP, and genomic DNA was sequenced to measure sgRNA abundance. The results showed that antigen expression and IL-2 complex treatment increased SMARTA Treg cell numbers by more than fivefold, and known Treg regulators like Il2ra and Icos were among the top hits, validating the model. Additionally, Rgs16 and Anxa2 were identified as candidate regulators of Treg cell abundance. The study provides a platform for identifying therapeutic targets in tumor-infiltrating Treg cells, which could enhance immunotherapy strategies. However, the evidence does not report limitations or evidence strength.

title: 778 CD7 signaling regulates survival of exhausted CD8 T cells

analysis.research_question_and_background: CD8+ T cell exhaustion is a major barrier to durable immune responses in cancer and chronic infection. The study aimed to explore the function of CD7 in maintaining the persistence of terminally exhausted CD8+ T cells during chronic antigen exposure.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study used the lymphocytic choriomeningitis virus (LCMV) model of chronic infection and multiple subcutaneous tumor models. It assessed CD7 expression and function through Cd7 deletion and overexpression, spectral flow cytometric phenotyping, bulk transcriptional profiling, and single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) of antigen-specific CD8+ T cells.
analysis.methods: To examine the signaling requirement for CD7 during terminal differentiation, the researchers restored CD7 signaling on Cd7-/- CD8 T cells using retroviral overexpression and compared wild type CD7 to CD7 with phosphomimetic mutations of key amino acids.
analysis.main_results: Conditional deletion of Cd7 during chronic infection markedly reduces the persistence and increases the apoptotic susceptibility of antigen-specific CD8+ T cells. Wild-type CD7 signaling improved persistence via reduced susceptibility to apoptosis, and increased expression of granzyme A and granzyme B.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: These data further explore the function of CD7 in maintaining the persistence of terminally exhausted CD8+ T cells during chronic antigen exposure, underscoring CD7’s importance in sustaining cytotoxic subsets of these cells.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that targeting the CD7 axis could enhance T cell persistence and function in chronic infection and cancer immunotherapy.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its use of a single model system, which may not fully represent the complexity of human immune responses. The evidence is moderate in strength due to the reliance on in vivo models and the absence of direct clinical outcomes.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the role of CD7 in maintaining the persistence of terminally exhausted CD8+ T cells during chronic antigen exposure. Using the lymphocytic choriomeningitis virus (LCMV) model and subcutaneous tumor models, the researchers assessed CD7 expression and function through genetic manipulation and advanced sequencing techniques. They found that CD7 deletion reduces T cell persistence and increases apoptosis, while wild-type CD7 signaling enhances survival and cytotoxic function. These results highlight CD7's importance in sustaining antiviral CD8+ T cell responses and suggest potential therapeutic strategies for chronic infections and cancer immunotherapy. However, the study's reliance on in vivo models limits its generalizability, and the evidence is considered moderate in strength.

title: 791 Cell-intrinsic sex differences shape exhausted CD8 + T cell fate

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to understand how biological sex influences CD8+ T cell differentiation and exhaustion, addressing a knowledge gap in the field of immunotherapy and cancer outcomes.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study used transgenic CD8+ T cells expressing a T cell receptor specific to lymphocytic choriomeningitis virus (LCMV) in multiple syngeneic models, evaluating male and female cells in chronic LCMV infection and B16F10 melanoma models.
analysis.methods: The researchers analyzed antigen-specific cells using multiparameter flow cytometry and single-cell RNA-sequencing to assess expansion, differentiation, and exhaustion states.
analysis.main_results: Male antigen-specific CD8+ T cells exhibited greater initial expansion and enhanced responsiveness to antigen stimulation, but also showed accelerated progression toward terminal exhaustion.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings demonstrate that donor sex influences both the magnitude and differentiation state of adoptively transferred CD8+ T cells, highlighting the importance of cell-intrinsic sex-specific programs in T cell fate decisions.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These observations suggest that intrinsic sex-dependent programs shape T cell fate following adoptive transfer and may represent an important consideration for the optimization of allogeneic cell-based immunotherapies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's limitations include the use of a single viral model and the need for further validation in different contexts, but the evidence is strong due to the use of multiple syngeneic models and comprehensive analysis methods.

analysis.summary_en: This study explored how biological sex affects CD8+ T cell differentiation and exhaustion, showing that male cells expand more efficiently but progress faster to terminal exhaustion, highlighting the importance of cell-intrinsic sex-specific programs in T cell fate.

title: 779 SLAMF7 downregulation in CD8 T cells delineates terminal exhaustion and associates with advanced disease in renal cell carcinoma

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to understand the role of SLAMF7 in CD8 T cell exhaustion, addressing the need to better define molecular programs distinguishing functional from terminally exhausted T cells in the context of chronic viral infection and cancer.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involved analyzing SLAMF7 expression in CD8 T cells across multiple experimental and clinical settings, including in vitro activation of mouse and human CD8 T cells, acute and chronic lymphocytic choriomeningitis virus (LCMV) infection, murine tumor models, and human renal cell carcinoma (RCC).
analysis.methods: SLAMF7 expression and CD8 T cell differentiation were assessed using phenotypic, transcriptional, and functional features. The study included in vitro activation of mouse and human CD8 T cells, acute and chronic LCMV infection, murine tumor models, and human RCC.
analysis.main_results: SLAMF7 was absent in naïve mouse and human CD8 T cells but was rapidly induced upon activation. Following acute LCMV infection, SLAMF7 was broadly expressed by effector and memory CD8 T cell subsets, with higher expression in more differentiated cytolytic populations. In contrast, under persistent antigenic stimulation, SLAMF7 was highly expressed in progenitor and transitory exhausted CD8 T cells but was downregulated in PD-1hi terminally exhausted cells. Loss of SLAMF7 expression coincided with increased inhibitory receptor and TOX expression, attenuation of cytotoxic programs, and impaired polyfunctional cytokine production.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: These findings identify SLAMF7 downregulation as a conserved feature of terminal CD8 T cell exhaustion across chronic infection, tumor models, and human RCC, suggesting SLAMF7 may serve as a biomarker of CD8 T cell immune competence and disease severity in solid tumors.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that SLAMF7 downregulation could be used to stratify immune states in RCC, potentially aiding in the identification of patients with more severe disease and guiding therapeutic strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's limitations include the use of non-randomized clinical samples and the need for further validation in larger cohorts. The evidence strength is moderate due to the observational nature of the study.

analysis.summary_en: This study analyzed SLAMF7 expression in CD8 T cells across various settings, identifying SLAMF7 downregulation as a marker of terminal exhaustion in RCC, which could inform immune competence and disease severity.

title: 797 Granzyme A is critical for the cytotoxic function of exhausted CD8 + T cells

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to understand the role of granzyme A (GzmA) in CD8+ T cell exhaustion, addressing the variability in response rates to cancer immunotherapies. Background CD8 + T cell exhaustion is a major contributor to the persistence of cancer, and while immunotherapies target exhausted T cells, response rates remain highly variable.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involved generating a novel murine Gzma-/- model by CRISPR/Cas9 and adoptively co-transferring both Gzma knockout (KO) and wild-type (WT) donor T cells into WT recipient mice infected with chronic lymphocytic choriomeningitis virus to explore the cell-intrinsic effects of GzmA deficiency over longitudinal progression of T cell exhaustion. The study also analyzed granzyme usage in multiple human tumor types using single-cell RNA-sequencing, flow cytometry, and multiplex ELISA.
analysis.methods: Methods included generating a Gzma-/- mouse model, adoptive transfer of T cells, and analysis of granzyme usage in human tumors using single-cell RNA-sequencing, flow cytometry, and multiplex ELISA. Multiplex ELISA confirmed high levels of GzmA protein in the tumor microenvironment, and single-cell RNA-sequencing demonstrated differential gene expression between GzmA KO and WT exhausted T cells.
analysis.main_results: In human tumors, GzmA was found to be the dominant T cell effector molecule. GzmA KO T cells exhibited a 41% deficit in cytotoxic capacity compared to WT T cells, while GzmB expression was upregulated in GzmA KO cells. These findings establish GzmA as a critical mediator of T cell cytotoxicity in exhausted CD8+ T cells.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study defines GzmA as a critical mediator of T cell cytotoxicity in CD8+ T cell exhaustion, highlighting its importance in cancer immunotherapies. GzmA is highly expressed in both human tumor-infiltrating T cells and murine exhausted T cells, and its knockout revealed that granzymes are coordinately regulated during T cell exhaustion.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings will crucially inform strategies to improve T cell cytotoxicity in cancer immunotherapies, as GzmA is an indispensable cytotoxic effector molecule in exhausted T cells.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's limitations include the use of a murine model and the need for further validation in human samples. The evidence strength is moderate due to the use of a non-human model and the need for additional clinical studies.

analysis.summary_en: The study identified granzyme A (GzmA) as a critical mediator of T cell cytotoxicity in exhausted CD8+ T cells, highlighting its importance in cancer immunotherapies. GzmA knockout revealed a 41% deficit in cytotoxic capacity, while GzmB expression was upregulated in GzmA KO cells, establishing GzmA as an indispensable cytotoxic effector molecule.
